Hi Amit —

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned after the call: 

Summary of needs (as discussed)
- Primary use case: intelligent customer support + KYC doc parsing (mixed short chat + multi-page doc ingestion).
- Traffic profile: expected 150k–300k monthly active users initially; peak concurrency unknown (you mentioned heavy daytime peaks).
- Latency SLO: 200–400ms for chat paths; batch document processing can be higher.
- Data controls: must ensure no customer data is used for model training; SOC2 + VPC options are required for production.

Deployment modes we're qualifying
1) Hosted API (Redwood-hosted): fastest to launch; pay-as-you-go per-token; ideal for pilot and early product-market fit.
2) Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool for predictable throughput and predictable monthly cost; good for production with steady traffic and isolation.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): required if you need private control plane, customer-managed networking, and stricter compliance (audit logs + KMS/HSM).

What I need from you to build a recommended cost model:
- Typical/average request sizes (tokens in prompt + completion) for chat and doc jobs
- Expected throughput (RPS) targets at peak and average
- % of traffic that must live in a private environment vs. OK to run on hosted
- Any vendor constraints (approved regions, minimum procurement windows)

Next steps
- If you can send the token/throughput numbers, I’ll run a Hosted vs Dedicated breakeven and a Private deployment estimate. I’ll include both per-token economics and reserved-capacity projections.
- I’ll also loop in our Solutions Engineer (Dev Patel) to build a short capacity plan and sample SOW.

I’m attaching a quick cost-modeling template + a short deployment comparison PDF to make the inputs easier.

If easier, we can do a quick 30-min follow-up tomorrow to walk through the worksheet. What time works for you?

Thanks,
Marissa

Amit — thanks for the numbers, this is exactly what I needed. I ran a quick, high-level preliminary comparison (see notes below) and attached the detailed worksheet for you to review. I’ve cc'd Dev (our SE) to build an ops/throughput plan next.

Preliminary cost guidance (very high level, conservative estimates):
- Hosted API (pay-as-you-go):
  - 10M tokens / month -> ~$300–$450/month
  - 50M tokens / month -> ~$1.5k–$2.2k/month
  - 100M tokens / month -> ~$3.0k–$4.4k/month
  - Pros: zero infra ops, instant scaling, best for pilot. Cons: unit cost higher at sustained scale and less isolation.

- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool):
  - Example commit: 1x dedicated A100-equivalent pool -> reserved $18k–$25k/month (varies by region and GPU type).
  - Breakeven: if you sustain >~300–600M effective tokens/month (depends on batching/quantization), Dedicated becomes more cost-effective. For your expected 80–120M tokens at month 6, Dedicated likely not the cheapest but offers predictable latency and strong isolation.
  - Options: burst capacity and hybrid routing (hosted for overflow).

- Private (VPC/on-prem):
  - One-time setup + ongoing infra management; pricing typically a platform fee + infra (we can provide model once we see region & vendor constraints).
  - Useful if you require private control plane and customer-managed KMS; higher TCO but meets compliance needs.

Notes and assumptions:
- Token cost in Hosted tier uses typical generative model pricing (prompt+response). Exact per-token rate depends on model family; I used a conservative mid-tier model for these estimates.
- Dedicated breakeven is sensitive to batching (document pipelines can be batched aggressively) and quantization (8-bit/4-bit optimizations).
- If you keep latency-critical chat on Dedicated and run heavy batch ingestion on Hosted (or scheduled Dedicated windows), you can optimize both cost and SLOs.

Attachments: cost-modeling-template.xlsx (filled with the above assumptions), deployment-comparison.pdf

Next steps I propose:
1) Dev to produce a capacity plan + example commit options and a short SOW draft (Dev — can you prepare this by EOD Friday?).
2) Amit — if you confirm a follow-up time, we’ll do a quick walkthrough of the worksheet and the SE plan.

I’ll prepare a clearer breakeven chart once we get your confirmation on the expected batching rates for docs.

Best,
Marissa
